text: Diener's seminal work defines SWB as the cognitive and affective evaluation of one's life, comprising life satisfaction and the relative absence of negative affect ( Diener, 1984 ). SWB is influenced by stable dispositional traits, e.g., personality, contextual elements, such as family and school climate, and dynamic regulatory processes. High SWB in adolescents correlates with improved academic performance and social adjustment ( Hernández-Torrano et al., 2025 ; Aldridge and McChesney, 2018 ).
source_label: Behavioral and computational perspectives on emotion regulation and subjective wellbeing: an integrative review with a focus on adolescents
